While the confidence intervals attempt to capture a wide range of probable outcomes, certain "tail events" or unforeseen shocks could push the actual results significantly outside these bounds. On the upside, a significant, unexpected positive development—such as a major technological breakthrough, a substantial policy change highly favorable to the underlying asset, or an unanticipated surge in demand—could cause the value to exceed the upper limits of my forecast. Conversely, outcomes could fall below the lower bounds due to severe, unforeseen negative events.
